title: Working at Redwood: Roles, Career Ladders, Benefits, Hiring & Onboarding, and Internal Tools
author: Samantha Reed
body:
Summary

This page consolidates key sections of the Redwood employee handbook focused on: what it means to work at Redwood, role definitions and career ladders, benefits and perks, a high-level hiring & onboarding overview, and a reference guide to the internal tools you will use day-to-day. It is intended for new hires, managers, and people-ops. For team-specific policies (time off, on-call rotas, technical interview recipes) see the linked pages under People Ops and Engineering.

--

1) Welcome: Working at Redwood

Introduction
Redwood is a developer-first platform built by engineers for engineers. Our values emphasize clarity, ownership, and high standards for reliability and performance. As an employee you should expect:
- Clear role expectations and an explicit career ladder.
- Regular performance conversations and documented growth plans.
- Access to tools, reimbursement, and flexible policies designed to help you do your best work.

Culture and working norms
- Asynchronous-first: Use documented RFCs and Confluence for decisions. Meetings should have agendas and clear outcomes.
- Blameless postmortems: Incidents are an opportunity to improve systems and processes.
- Ownership: Teams own their services end-to-end, including SLAs, runbooks, and cost targets.

Code of conduct
All employees must follow the Redwood Code of Conduct (see People Ops portal). Violations should be reported to people-ops or through the anonymous reporting channel.

--

2) Roles and Career Ladders (high level)

Purpose
Our ladders give transparency on expectations for individual contributors (IC) and managers across engineering, product, and go-to-market. Managers are evaluated both on technical/product outcomes and on coaching / people development.

Common role families
- Engineering: SWE I, SWE II, Senior SWE, Staff SWE, Principal SWE.
- Platform / Infra: same ladder names, with expectations for systems design, reliability, and cross-team influence.
- Product: Associate PM, PM, Senior PM, Group PM, Director of Product.
- Go-to-market: SDR, AE, Manager, Director.
- IC vs Manager paths: We support dual-track progression; an IC can reach Principal without becoming a people manager.

Level expectations (condensed table)
| Level | Typical years | Core expectations | Impact scope |
|-------|---------------|------------------|--------------|
| IC-1 / SWE I | 0-2 | Deliver features with guidance, write tests | Single service/feature |
| IC-2 / SWE II | 2-5 | Independently owns features, mentors juniors | Cross-service |
| Senior | 5+ | System design, ambiguous problems, drive projects | Multi-team |
| Staff | 8+ | Technical leadership, drive architecture, mentor leaders | Org-wide |
| Principal | 12+ | Strategic influence, define company technical directions | Company-wide |

Promotion process (summary)
1. Manager or peer nominates candidate with evidence against ladder rubric.
2. Candidate compiles a promotion packet (summary, examples, metrics, reviewer list).
3. Calibration panel reviews packet and provides recommendation.
4. Final decision communicated, with a written growth plan if not approved.

Promotion timelines and ownership
- Employees are typically eligible for promotion review once every 12 months.
- Managers and people-ops share ownership of process: managers prepare packets; people-ops runs logistics and panels.

--

3) Benefits and Perks (high level)

Health and wellness
- Medical, dental, and vision plans with Redwood covering a substantial portion of premiums.
- Mental health benefits including therapy reimbursement and an Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

Time off and leaves
- Generous paid time off (PTO) with recommended minimums.
- Parental leave (primary and secondary caregiver policies) and caregiver leave.
- Paid public holidays, and floating holidays for cultural observance.

Financial and retirement
- Competitive salary bands, equity grants on hire and periodic refreshes.
- 401(k) plan with company match where applicable.

Professional growth and learning
- Annual learning allowance for conferences, books, and courses.
- Mentorship program and quarterly hack days.

Work environment and hardware
- Remote-first with structured stipends for home office setup; per-role allowances for multi-monitor or docking station purchases.
- Travel stipend for quarterly in-person team meetings where applicable.

Perks and culture benefits
- Regular all-hands, town halls, and offsites.
- Team budgets for social events, and a monthly wellness stipend.

How to access benefits
- All benefits are available through the People Ops portal. For questions contact people-ops via the internal ticketing system.

--

4) Hiring & Onboarding Overview

Objectives
- Hire for skills and potential while minimizing bias.
- Provide new hires with a fast and consistent path to productivity.

Hiring stages (engineered for candidate experience)
1. Requisition and role rubric creation (hiring manager + recruiting).
2. Sourcing and screening (recruiter screens for fit and logistics).
3. Technical interview loop / role-specific assessments.
4. Hiring committee review and calibration.
5. Offer, compensation, and background checks.
6. Offer acceptance and pre-boarding.

Interview best practices
- Use standardized scorecards anchored to rubric.
- Interviewers must be trained on fairness and unconscious bias.
- Feedback deadlines: submit within 48 hours of interview.

Onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
1. Pre-boarding (IT account creation, offer paperwork, equipment shipment).
2. Day 1: Orientation (company values, benefits overview, security training).
3. Week 1: Team introductions, mentor pairing, first small ticket.
4. Month 1: Deliver first PR/feature, 1:1 with manager to set goals.
5. Month 3: Performance check-in and role clarity review.

New manager responsibilities
- Ensure first-week schedule, introductions to cross-functional partners, and an initial 90-day success plan.

Exit and offboarding
- Standard offboarding includes knowledge transfer, deprovisioning of accounts via IT, and an exit interview. People Ops owns the process and timeline.

--

5) Internal Tools Guide (quick reference)

Core tools and primary owners
- Slack (Communication) — Eng & GTM teams.
- Okta (SSO) — Security & IT.
- G Suite (Email/Drive) — Productivity.
- GitHub (Code hosting) — Engineering (repo owners maintain access lists).
- Linear (Issue tracking) — Product & Eng teams.
- Notion / Confluence (Documentation) — People Ops & Docs team.
- rwctl (internal CLI for deploys and runtime routing) — Eng Platform (team: eng-platform@redwood.example).
- Observability dashboards (Grafana/Datadog) — Eng-SRE.

Access and permissions
- All access requests start in the IT ticketing portal and are approved by resource owners.
- Principle of least privilege: request only the roles you need; temporary elevated access is preferred to permanent admin access.

Common workflows
- Onboarding: recruiter opens IT ticket to provision Okta, GitHub membership, Slack, G Suite and initial Linear permissions.
- Deploys: follow the rwctl CLI runbook (see eng-platform/runbooks) and request canary windows on the deployment calendar.
- Incident comms: use the #incident Slack channel and follow the incident runbook (oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process).

Self-service tips
- Passwords and secrets: store in company vault (refer to security-and-compliance/rbac-and-auth).
- Templates: use the team onboarding checklist templates in Confluence to accelerate new-hire ramp.

--

6) Manager & People Ops Playbook (short)

Performance cycles
- Quarterly check-ins with documented notes and an annual performance review.
- Managers must write clear role expectations within first 30 days.

Compensation adjustments
- Compensation reviews are coordinated with Finance and People Ops and follow the published cadence.

Policy exceptions
- Any exceptions (extended leave, pay adjustments outside bands) require written approval from People Ops and Finance.

--

7) Frequently Asked Questions

Q: Who do I contact for IT hardware issues?
A: Open an IT ticket via the People Ops portal and tag Eng Tools.

Q: How often can I request professional development funds?
A: Annual allowance; exceptions considered by People Ops.

Q: Where are promotion rubrics stored?
A: Promotion rubrics and sample packets are stored in Confluence under People Ops -> Promotions.

--

Ownership and feedback
